focus_summary.purpose: Eliminate unnecessary 'Would you like me to continue?' interruptions by using Claude Haiku to judge whether continuation is appropriate
key_flows: Stop hook intercepts Claude's stop attempts
Context extraction from last 10 transcript entries
Hook blocks or approves the stop based on evaluation
constraints: Must be fast (using Haiku for latency)
Throttling prevents infinite loops (3 continues per 5 minutes)
risks_or_unknowns: LLM evaluation can vary between runs
Token costs accumulate with heavy use
Hook system changes in Claude Code could break plugin

content.summary: Improve the quality and transparency of continuation decisions through better context and scoring
content.problem: Current decisions are binary with limited visibility into why the hook decided to continue or stop
content.scope: Judge prompt improvements, confidence scoring, and context enhancement
success_criteria: Users can see confidence levels for each decision
content.notes: Core to building user trust in the plugin

content.summary: Make the plugin more reliable through fallbacks, adaptive behavior, and observability
content.problem: Plugin depends on API availability and fixed throttling may not suit all workloads
content.scope: Offline fallback, adaptive throttling, health monitoring
success_criteria: Plugin works gracefully when API is unavailable
Health metrics are accessible for debugging

content.summary: Improve the developer experience for debugging, testing, and configuring the plugin
content.problem: Debugging hook behavior requires manual inspection of throttle files and logs
success_criteria: Developers can preview hook decisions without executing
Configuration can be done via natural language
content.notes: Moonshot NL config may require significant experimentation

work_items.title: Add Confidence Scoring to Continuation Decisions

content.summary: Extend the judge prompt to return a confidence score (0-100) alongside the continue/stop decision, surfacing this in the hook output for better debugging and user trust
implementation_steps: Update JSON schema in judge prompt to include confidence field (0-100)
Modify prompt to ask Claude to rate its confidence in the decision
Parse confidence from response JSON
Include confidence in the reason field of hook output
Add confidence thresholds for edge cases (e.g., <30% = allow stop even if continue suggested)
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Judge returns confidence score 0-100 with every decision
- [ ] Confidence appears in hook output reason field
- [ ] Low confidence (<30%) decisions default to stop
- [ ] All existing eval scenarios pass with confidence included

test_plan.description: Add confidence field validation to existing scenarios

content.risk_mitigation: Confidence is additive—existing logic unchanged if parsing fails

content.summary: Read the current TodoWrite todo list state and include it in the context sent to the judge, allowing smarter continuation decisions based on pending work items
implementation_steps: Identify where Claude Code stores TodoWrite state (likely in session data)
Add logic to extract pending todos from session/transcript
Include pending todo count and titles in judge context
Update judge prompt to consider todos as strong continuation signal
Add scenarios testing todo-aware decisions
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Hook extracts pending todos from available state
- [ ] Judge prompt includes todo context section
- [ ] Zero todos with completion signals bias toward stop

test_plan.description: Add scenarios with various todo states
Test todo extraction from real sessions

content.risk_mitigation: Fallback to current behavior if todo state unavailable

content.summary: Add a dry-run mode that evaluates what the hook would decide without actually blocking or approving, useful for debugging and testing new scenarios
implementation_steps: Add REDBULL_DRY_RUN environment variable check
In dry-run mode, run evaluation but always return approve
Log the would-be decision to stderr or a debug file
Document dry-run usage in README
Add test helper that uses dry-run mode
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Would-be decision is logged for inspection

test_plan.description: Test dry-run mode outputs expected logs

content.risk_mitigation: Completely additive, no impact on normal operation

content.summary: Add a simple heuristic-based fallback for when the Claude API is unavailable, using keyword matching on transcript to make basic continue/stop decisions
implementation_steps: Detect API failure (timeout, network error, non-200 response)
Implement keyword-based heuristics (e.g., 'TODO', 'next', 'then' = continue)
Implement stop keywords (e.g., 'complete', 'done', 'finished', 'ready')
Log when fallback is used for debugging
Add eval scenarios testing heuristic accuracy
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Heuristics achieve >70% accuracy on eval suite
- [ ] Fallback is faster than API call

test_plan.description: Run eval suite in offline mode
Simulate API failure and verify fallback

content.risk_mitigation: Heuristics are conservative—bias toward stopping on uncertainty

content.summary: Replace fixed 3/5min throttle with adaptive limits based on session characteristics like task complexity, continuation success rate, and user activity patterns
implementation_steps: Track continuation outcomes (was the continue productive?)
Calculate success rate over rolling window
Increase limit (up to 6) for high success rate sessions
Decrease limit (down to 2) for low success rate sessions
Persist adaptive state per session
Add observability for throttle adjustments
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Throttle limit adjusts based on success rate

test_plan.description: Simulate sessions with varying success rates

content.risk_mitigation: Bounds on limits (2-6) prevent runaway behavior

experiment.small_experiment: Implement basic success tracking and log suggested throttle adjustments without applying them
experiment.success_metric: Correlation between success rate and suggested throttle changes
experiment.rollback_plan: Disable adaptive logic via environment variable, revert to fixed 3/5min

content.summary: Add structured logging and metrics collection for hook execution times, decision distributions, API latency, and error rates
implementation_steps: Create structured log format (JSON lines)
Log hook invocations with timestamps
Log decision type and latency
Log API call duration and status
Create simple stats command to analyze logs
Document log location and format
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] All hook invocations are logged in structured format
content.risk_mitigation: Logging is opt-in or bounded to prevent disk issues

content.summary: Replace fixed 'last 10 entries' with intelligent context selection that prioritizes task-defining messages, recent tool outputs, and continuation signals while reducing token usage
implementation_steps: Identify message types (user request, tool output, assistant response)
Weight messages by recency and relevance
Always include initial task request
Include last 3 assistant messages regardless
Prioritize messages with todo/task keywords
Cap total tokens to optimize cost

test_plan.description: Compare accuracy with old vs new selection

content.risk_mitigation: A/B test against fixed selection before full rollout

experiment.small_experiment: Log both fixed and smart context for 50 decisions, compare token counts and accuracy
experiment.rollback_plan: Environment variable to revert to fixed 10-entry selection

content.summary: Allow users to configure plugin behavior via natural language comments in their CLAUDE.md or session, e.g., 'continue aggressively' or 'stop for every file change'
implementation_steps: Define supported configuration intents (aggressive, conservative, balanced)
Scan CLAUDE.md for redbull configuration comments
Parse intent using simple keyword matching first
If ambiguous, use Claude to interpret intent
Apply configuration as judge prompt modifiers
Cache parsed config per session
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Invalid config is ignored with warning

test_plan.description: Test config parsing for known phrases
Test decision bias with different configs

content.risk_mitigation: Start with simple keyword matching, graduate to LLM parsing

experiment.small_experiment: Implement keyword-only parsing for 3 presets (aggressive, balanced, conservative) and measure usage
experiment.success_metric: >20% of users customize after feature announcement
experiment.rollback_plan: Remove config parsing, revert to default balanced behavior
